description.value: A rough-out for a brine-channel cutting blade, struck from a single chert nodule and abandoned before grinding because the fourth blow found a flaw the maker had not seen. Blanks were made in quantity at the working floors and finished only as the cuts required them, so an abandoned blank is a record of a working day rather than of a failure. About twelve hundred were left lying when the companies dissolved in 2295 and they have not been disturbed since. This is the best preserved of the eleven collected and by some way the least interesting.

notes.value: The document filed with it is a company salt account listing the batch, the floor and the day's output. Two thirds of the accounts left in the cuts are still legible, which is two thirds more than the shipping records of the concession that employed the companies.
